newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoran island separatists agree to dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Comoran island separatists agree to dialogue.

text.p: Secessionists on the Comoran island of Moheli said on Thursday they had agreed to hold talks with government officials.
Mahmoud Said Manine, "finance minister" of a breakaway Moheli administration named on Wednesday, told Reuters by telephone the secessionists agreed to talks at a neutral venue.
The meeting would bring together separatists from the islands of Moheli and Anjouan and the Comoran government and its opposition.
On Wednesday, the secessionists had objected to talks in a meeting with Organisation of African Unity (OAU) mediator Pierre Yere.
Manine said the Moheli separatists demanded an international force be stationed on the Indian Ocean island.
"The OAU delegation agreed to the principle of an intervention force," said Manine. There was no immediate comment available from the OAU team, which met government officials on Thursday.
The Moheli secessionists released on Wednesday a list of its self-declared government including a high school teacher as its foreign minister and Manine, an economist, as finance minister.
Secessionists on Moheli, the smallest of the three islands in the Islamic Republic of the Comoros, appointed a 75-year-old former Islamic preacher as "president" on Monday after weeks of unrest.
Anjouan, the second largest island, broke away early this month. The Comoro Islands have a population of some 670,000.

Islanders on Anjouan and Moheli say they want to return to French rule or become independent because they have received little from the government but poverty and numerous coups since Comoran independence from France in 1975.
The poverty in the three islands of Comoros contrasts with comparative prosperity on the island of Mayotte, which voted against independence in 1975 and remains under French rule.
France has denounced the secessionist unrest, saying it could destabilise the whole region.
